speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scarlet Fever (confirmed by recent viral prodrome and subsequent rash distribution, though Strep A is the primary concern). REQUEST TEST: Throat_Culture, ASO_Titer. REQUEST IMAGES: Full_body_skin_rash_photo_to_check_for_pastia_lines_and_strawberry_tongue.
